# Current Capabilities And Limitations

This page is generated from the checked-in capability declaration and
source-consistency checks. It distinguishes available components, integrated
behavior, original proof and unverified gaps. A generated label alone is
not a runtime owner or exact-candidate acceptance witness; roadmaps and
architecture intent do not override current source.

**Maturity:** Experimental alpha; substantial implementation, but no general production-support or backward-compatibility guarantee on 0.x.

## Product boundary

A self-managed distributed runtime with an integrated, partitioned SQL storage layer; not a plug-in for an existing PostgreSQL cluster.

The rows used by a data-local operation must live in Lagrange partitions.

## Data and query model

| Capability | Current state |
| --- | --- |
| Table partitioning | range-based |
| Default replica count | 3 |
| Partition consensus | raft |
| Partition consensus backend | Raft-rs WASM operation port |
| Runtime-service Cell consensus | none; durable state uses ordinary replicated tables |
| Secondary indexes | Partition-local SQLite B-tree indexes supported; no cross-partition routing narrowing |
| Global secondary indexes | No |
| Locking reads | Partition-row reservation with fail-fast 55P03 conflict refusal |
| Live query subscriptions | Admin WebSocket supported |

## Public service path

The deployment model is [Artifact / Binding / Cell](vocabulary.md#service-deployment-hierarchy).
Recommended authoring: **Code-first JavaScript service compiler**.
Managed WASM execution: **Genuine WASI component Cell**.

Lagrange exposes one service API across execution providers. Provider choice may
change packaging, isolation, and the final runtime adapter; it must not create a
second Artifact / Binding / Cell model or change handler, distributed-call,
`run`, `emit`, reduction, routing, budget, retry, or invocation-identity
semantics.

Binding source kinds are publicly invocable: `request`, `call`; accepted
`change`, `time`, `once`, `boot`, `pushdown` kinds
may be declared but have no public invocation adapter.
Managed OCI activation remains unsupported. When OCI execution is implemented,
it must project the same service API rather than introduce a provider-specific
programming model.

| Call property | Current state |
| --- | --- |
| Selector | Literal single-table SELECT fixed at deployment |
| Selector interpolation | No |
| Default rows per shard | 4096 |
| Default emits per shard run | 64 |
| Default coordinated partial entries | 1024 |
| Default concurrent shard runs | 8 |
| Same-host shard runs | Serialized per component instance |
| Partial values | Finite numbers |
| Partial keys | Must be disjoint across shards |
| Nested calls per HTTP request | 1 |
| Global cross-partition snapshot | No |
| Caller cancellation | No |
| Direct-call caller idempotency key | No |

Supported lifecycle SQL:

- `INSTALL SERVICE $1;`
- `UPGRADE SERVICE $1;`
- `REMOVE SERVICE $1;`
- `SHOW SERVICE $1;`
- `SHOW SERVICES;`
- `CONFIGURE SERVICE ACCESS $1;`
- `CREATE BINDING $1;`
- `CALL BINDING $1;`

| Execution provider | External installation | Managed execution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `wasm_component` | External install through lifecycle SQL | Genuine WASI component Cell |
| `oci_container` | Unsupported | Descriptor and in-memory lifecycle scaffold only |

WASM is the current supported execution provider. OCI remains a future provider;
its packaging and isolation differ, but its application semantics do not.

## Embedded application sessions

The package exports a side-effect-free `createEmbeddedLagrange` factory. A
started handle opens application sessions over the runtime's canonical SQL
engine and supports callback transactions with serialized statements, typed
failures, rollback before commit, and expired callback handles. Application
identifiers isolate transaction session identity; they are not table, tenant,
schema, or authorization boundaries. Transaction-control SQL is reserved for
the callback API. The current lifecycle permits one runtime start per process
lifetime.

Code that constructs `BootstrapService` or `NodeJoiningService` directly
must first reserve the node's boot incarnation with the exported
`reserveBootIncarnation(dataDir)` and pass it as `bootIncarnation`; both
constructors refuse its absence.

## Replication and recovery

| Capability | Current state |
| --- | --- |
| SQLite partition checkpoint creation | Active for file-backed SQLite partitions |
| SQLite partition snapshot transfer/install | Active for file-backed SQLite partitions |
| SQLite partition proof-gated log compaction | Active for file-backed SQLite partitions |
| Automatic partition checkpoint cadence | Active for file-backed SQLite partitions |
| Integrated replica recovery on raft-rs | Active for file-backed SQLite partitions |
| Message-group log compaction | Unsupported |
| Learner promotion | Leader match-index progress proof after initial scheduling delay |
| Raft votes, appended entries and snapshots | Synced to disk before any dependent message is sent (survives power loss) |

Component presence, automatic execution, and published recovery SLAs are distinct
claims. File-backed SQLite user partitions run automatic raft-rs checkpoint
cadence, proof-gated log compaction, and lagging-follower snapshot catch-up;
control-plane partitions and message groups remain excluded from compaction, and
snapshot recovery is internal replica repair rather than a user backup or PITR
product.

- Compatibility claim: bounded measured SQL slice, not complete PostgreSQL or ORM compatibility

## Important limitations

| Area | Limitation |
| --- | --- |
| Query routing | Production partition narrowing effectively requires a key column named id; other predicates may scatter to every partition. |
| Query routing | Unified UTF-8 byte-order (BINARY) key comparison across split keys and routing keys ensures consistent placement and query routing, failing closed on unsupported mixed-type key comparisons. |
| Indexes | Partition-local B-tree secondary indexes (CREATE INDEX / DROP INDEX) are created and maintained per partition SQLite database via IndexService to accelerate local partition scans, while global secondary indexes across partitions are unsupported and secondary indexes do not narrow cross-partition routing (queries without id still scatter). |
| SQL writes | A SQL write whose proposal reached consensus but whose outcome the serving replica cannot confirm is re-delivered under its own entry identity (backing off to 2 s) until the statement deadline, or query.timeoutMs (30 s) when the caller passed none, and then fails typed as partition_write_outcome_unknown; it may have applied. Re-issuing it is safe only under the same idempotency key, which the PostgreSQL wire and embedded application database surfaces do not yet accept. |
| Replication | SQLite-backed message-group raft-rs logs still grow without bounded compaction and recover by full replay; they do not yet use the partition snapshot compaction lifecycle. |
| Replication | Learner promotion waits for an initial scheduling delay and then requires a current-leader match-index progress proof against the safe promotion index before voting. |
| Replication | A replica held in _raft_rs_replica_lifecycle with reason = 'reseed-required' after proven history loss stays out of consensus permanently; there is no automatic reseed procedure yet, and replacement requires fresh-replica-identity ADD/REPLACE/REMOVE. |
| Replication | Only what Raft promises to peers (a vote, appended log entries, a snapshot) and the replica lifecycle row are synced to disk before they are acknowledged; other writes (commit index, applied progress, application rows) survive a process crash but may roll back on power loss and are re-applied from the synced log. A disk that acknowledges a flush from a volatile write cache without power-loss protection voids the power-loss guarantee. |
| Storage lifecycle | Replica cleanup and recreation are durably serialized by services.service_id. A directory-local SQLite ownership lock rejects a second live OS process before provenance, rejoin, or replica storage activity. |
| Service execution | Request and call Bindings are publicly invocable. Change, time, once, boot, and pushdown Bindings may be declared but have no public invocation adapter. |
| Service execution | A call selects one bounded shard batch; the public path does not stream or page an unbounded partition scan. |
| Service execution | Coordinated partial values are finite numbers and their keys must be disjoint across shards. |
| Service portability | Managed OCI container activation is unsupported; the recommended service path is a WASI component. |
| PostgreSQL compatibility | Password authentication and TLS are implemented, but SCRAM and arbitrary PostgreSQL or ORM compatibility are not claimed. |
| PostgreSQL compatibility | The listener speaks the PostgreSQL wire protocol with a restricted SQL dialect; ORM and psql meta-command compatibility are not claimed. Statements drivers commonly send at startup or for introspection fail: SHOW <setting>, SET, RESET, DISCARD ALL, DEALLOCATE, version(), current_database(), current_setting(), pg_catalog tables, plain EXPLAIN, DROP TABLE, WITH ... SELECT/INSERT/DELETE, IN (subquery) and VALUES (...) as a query. |
| SQL | A query text that holds more than one statement is refused whole and none of it runs: SQLSTATE 0A000 over the PostgreSQL wire, error code MULTIPLE_STATEMENTS_UNSUPPORTED through the application database. Send each statement separately; trailing semicolons and comments are accepted. |
| SQL | INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE with RETURNING are refused (SQLSTATE 0A000, "RETURNING is not supported") and nothing is applied; read generated values with a separate SELECT. INSERT ... SELECT is refused the same way ("INSERT ... SELECT is not supported"). |
| SQL | Transaction control is BEGIN [WORK, TRANSACTION] or START TRANSACTION, optionally with the READ WRITE mode; COMMIT or END [WORK, TRANSACTION]; and ROLLBACK or ABORT [WORK, TRANSACTION]. Comments outside quotes are allowed anywhere in these statements. The other PostgreSQL transaction modes (isolation levels, READ ONLY, DEFERRABLE and NOT DEFERRABLE) are refused with SQLSTATE 0A000, naming the mode, because the engine does not provide them: a block cannot be made read-only or given a stated isolation level. The statement must be the whole query text: a transaction keyword followed by anything else (BEGIN followed by an INSERT with no semicolon) is a syntax error (SQLSTATE 42601) and nothing runs. Savepoints, COMMIT AND CHAIN and prepared transactions are not supported. ROLLBACK or COMMIT with no transaction in progress answers its command tag with a WARNING (SQLSTATE 25P01), as PostgreSQL does. Closing the connection inside a transaction block rolls the transaction back at once. |
| PostgreSQL compatibility | Drivers that send plain BEGIN, START TRANSACTION or BEGIN READ WRITE work. A driver that adds READ ONLY, an isolation level or DEFERRABLE to BEGIN gets SQLSTATE 0A000 and no transaction is begun. pgjdbc with setReadOnly(true) sends BEGIN READ ONLY, which includes Spring @Transactional(readOnly = true); set the pgjdbc connection property readOnlyMode=ignore to keep plain BEGIN. psycopg and SQLAlchemy send a mode only when an isolation level or read-only is configured on the connection or engine. Older asyncpg versions and some Npgsql versions send an isolation level on BEGIN. These driver behaviours are untested here; they come from driver documentation. |
| SQL | An explicit transaction has a 60-second budget from BEGIN. When the budget runs out before COMMIT, the server rolls the transaction back within about a second. After that, any later statement in that block, including a new BEGIN, is refused with SQLSTATE 25P04 and never runs outside the transaction; the block is then failed until ROLLBACK, or until a COMMIT, which answers ROLLBACK. A COMMIT of a transaction that expired before COMMIT fails with SQLSTATE 25P04 stating that no changes were committed, and leaves the session idle. A COMMIT that fails after it began committing (for example, the budget ran out while the partitions of a multi-partition transaction were committing) answers SQLSTATE 08007 (transaction_resolution_unknown): some changes may have been committed. Known limitation: in that case the transaction can be left partly committed. If the block is still open after an 08007, the ROLLBACK that ends it carries a WARNING that the previous transaction's outcome is unknown. The embedded application database behaves the same way: a statement of transaction(callback) after the budget ran out is refused (NO_TRANSACTION), and a COMMIT that may have been partly applied rejects with TRANSACTION_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN. |
| SQL | SQL INSERT and UPDATE statements evaluate supported expressions, safely escape string literals, and preserve dollar-quoted strings ($$...$$, $tag$...$tag$); unsupported AST expression nodes fail closed with a typed error before mutation. |
| SQL | CREATE TABLE enforces PRIMARY KEY (including composite PRIMARY KEY), UNIQUE, and CHECK constraints per partition; FOREIGN KEY and REFERENCES declarations across distributed partitions are explicitly refused before creation. |
| Security | Internal cluster HTTP ingress on /cluster/state, /bootstrap, and /register-service enforces HTTP authentication when credentials are configured, while /livez, /startupz, and /readyz remain probe-accessible. |
| SQL | INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING is supported (translating to INSERT OR IGNORE) and skips conflicting rows as PostgreSQL does. INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE is refused before mutation with SQLSTATE 0A000 (UNSUPPORTED_SQL_FEATURE); use ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING or a separate UPDATE statement. |
| Transactions | SELECT ... FOR UPDATE provides partition-row reservation with fail-fast 55P03 conflict refusal, rollback release, and session budget timeout; it does not provide full serializable isolation or waiting lock queues. |
| Streaming & CDC | Live-query subscriptions over Admin WebSocket are active, while external CDC consumption on user tables (subscribeTable, subscribeTables, and CDCManager user-table streaming) remains disabled and unsupported in the initial stable core (CDC_EVENT_STREAM_DISABLED, Decision D2); internal replicated projection and message-group CDC obligations operate through the internal durable occurrence ledger. Evidenced in docs/migration.md, architecture/postgres-wire.md, and src/cdc/cdc-integration-service.js. |
| Security | Node-to-node transport is plain WebSocket without cryptographic peer authentication; deploy it only on a trusted private network. |
| Operations | Backup/restore/PITR and a supported rolling-upgrade contract are not available on 0.x. |
| Operations | In-place upgrade is unsupported from any pre-0.2.6 build that moved a message-group replica to a joining node under its existing replica name: every release through 0.2.5 (npm 0.1.1, 0.2.4-rc.0 to rc.2 and 0.2.5; Docker 0.1.0, 0.1.1, 0.2.4-rc.2 and 0.2.5) and main before the 0.2.6 identity-reuse fix. A node holding a message-group replica whose name it did not create can elect a second leader and lose acknowledged writes after the upgrade; rebuild such clusters or dump and restore them. |
| Replication | Automatic partition checkpoint cadence (10,000 entries or 256 MiB pending log bytes), proof-gated _raft_rs_log compaction, and lagging-follower snapshot catch-up are active for file-backed SQLite user partitions on raft-rs. Control-plane system partitions and message groups remain excluded from snapshot compaction, and partition snapshots are internal replica repair rather than a user backup/PITR product or published RPO/RTO SLA. |
| PostgreSQL compatibility | SQL INSERT and UPDATE expression evaluation supports safe string literal escaping, dollar-quoted strings, arithmetic, type casts, and functions, while unsupported AST nodes fail closed with SQLSTATE 0A000 before mutation. |
| Transactions | Public PostgreSQL-wire callers have no general idempotency-key/retry contract. A timeout or lost reply can leave COMMIT outcome unknown; do not infer rollback or retry an ambiguous mutation blindly. |
